      const messages = [{ role: "user" as const, content: "Return JSON." }];
      
      test("NVIDIA NIM builds an OpenAI-compatible request without native JSON mode", () => {
        const adapter = new NvidiaNimChatAdapter({
          apiKey: "test-key",
          model: "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
        });
      
        const params = adapter.buildRequestParams({
          messages,
          maxTokens: 512,
          structuredOutput: { type: "json_object" },
        });
      
        assert.equal(params.model, "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct");
        assert.equal(params.max_tokens, 512);
        assert.equal(params.response_format, undefined);
        assert.deepEqual(params.messages, messages);
      });
      
      test("NVIDIA NIM exposes its provider and model identity", () => {
        const adapter = new NvidiaNimChatAdapter({
          apiKey: "test-key",
          model: "qwen/qwen3-32b",
        });
      
        assert.equal(adapter.providerKey, "nvidia-nim");
        assert.equal(adapter.model, "qwen/qwen3-32b");
        assert.equal(adapter.runtimeIdentity?.provider, "nvidia-nim");
      });
      
      test("NVIDIA NIM maps an OpenAI-compatible completion to the shared response", async () => {
        const adapter = new NvidiaNimChatAdapter({
          apiKey: "test-key",
          model: "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
        });
        (adapter as unknown as { client: unknown }).client = {
          chat: {
            completions: {
              create: async () => ({
                id: "chatcmpl-nvidia-1",
                model: "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
                choices: [
                  {
                    index: 0,
                    message: { role: "assistant", content: "{\"verified\":true}" },
                    finish_reason: "stop",
                  },
                ],
                usage: { prompt_tokens: 12, completion_tokens: 8, total_tokens: 20 },
              }),
            },
          },
        };
      
        const response = await adapter.complete({
          messages,
          maxTokens: 512,
          structuredOutput: { type: "json_object" },
        });
      
        assert.equal(response.provider, "nvidia-nim");
        assert.equal(response.model, "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct");
        assert.equal(response.choices[0]?.message.content, '{"verified":true}');
        assert.equal(response.usage.totalTokens, 20);
      });
      
      test("NVIDIA NIM availability probe uses the configured base URL without exposing the key", async () => {
        const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;
        let requestedUrl = "";
        let authorization = "";
        globalThis.fetch = (async (input, init) => {
          requestedUrl = String(input);
          authorization = new Headers(init?.headers).get("authorization") ?? "";
          return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
        }) as typeof fetch;
      
        try {
          const adapter = new NvidiaNimChatAdapter({
            apiKey: "test-key",
            baseUrl: "https://nvidia.test.invalid/v1/",
            model: "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
          });
      
          const availability = await adapter.checkAvailability();

          assert.equal(availability.reason, undefined);
          assert.equal(requestedUrl, "https://nvidia.test.invalid/v1/models");
          assert.equal(authorization, "Bearer test-key");
        } finally {
          globalThis.fetch = originalFetch;
        }
      });

      function recomposeSupportedClaims(results: readonly SemanticClaimVerification[]): string {
        return results
          .filter((result) => result.state === "SUPPORTED")
          .map((result) => {
            const text = result.text.trim();
            return /[.!?ØŸ]$/u.test(text) ? text : `${text}.`;
          })
          .join("\n");
      }
      
      export class CitationSemanticVerificationService implements CitationSemanticVerifier {
        constructor(
          private readonly model: ModelAdapter,
          private readonly maxUnknownRetries = MAX_UNKNOWN_RETRIES,
        ) {}
      
        private async completeClaims(
          input: {
            claims: readonly PreparedSemanticClaim[];
            evidence: readonly CitationSemanticEvidence[];
            questionText: string;
            thresholdComparisons: unknown[];
          },
          budget: SemanticTokenBudget,
        ): Promise<ModelCompletionResponse | null> {
          const messages = buildSemanticVerificationMessages({
            claims: input.claims.map((claim) => claim.text),
            evidence: input.evidence,
            currentQuestion: input.questionText,
            thresholdComparisons: input.thresholdComparisons,
          });
      
          const estimatedPromptTokens = estimateSemanticPromptTokens(messages);
          const finiteBudget = Number.isFinite(budget.remainingTotalTokens);
      
          if (
            finiteBudget &&
            budget.remainingTotalTokens <= estimatedPromptTokens
          ) {
            return null;

I’m going to add a bounded completion timeout with a regression test, then compare Nemotron Super under that bound.       const MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS = 86_400;
      
      type ProviderErrorShape = {
        status?: unknown;
        statusCode?: unknown;
        code?: unknown;
        name?: unknown;
        headers?: unknown;
        error?: unknown;
      };
      
      function record(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
        return typeof value === "object" && value !== null
          ? value as Record<string, unknown>
          : null;
      }
      
      function stringField(value: unknown): string | null {
        return typeof value === "string" ? value : null;
      }
      
      function numericStatus(value: unknown): number | null {
        return typeof value === "number" && Number.isInteger(value) ? value : null;
      }
      
      function headerValue(headers: unknown, name: string): string | null {
        if (headers instanceof Headers) return headers.get(name);
        const values = record(headers);
        if (!values) return null;
        const value = values[name] ?? values[name.toLowerCase()] ?? values[name.toUpperCase()];
        return typeof value === "string" ? value : null;
      }
      
      function parseRetryAfterSeconds(value: string | null): number | undefined {
        if (!value) return undefined;
        const seconds = Number(value);
        if (Number.isFinite(seconds) && seconds > 0) {
          return Math.min(MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS, Math.ceil(seconds));
        }
        const retryAt = Date.parse(value);
        if (!Number.isFinite(retryAt)) return undefined;
        const remaining = Math.ceil((retryAt - Date.now()) / 1000);
        return remaining > 0 ? Math.min(MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS, remaining) : undefined;
      }
      
      export function mapLlmProviderError(error: unknown): AppError {
        // AppErrors are already the controlled, sanitized error type. Pass every
        // AppError through unchanged so the provider boundary preserves precise
        // codes/status codes (e.g. validation 4xx) instead of collapsing them.
        if (error instanceof AppError) {
          return error;
        }
      
        const outer = (record(error) ?? {}) as ProviderErrorShape;
        const nested = record(outer.error);
        // Providers disagree on the field name: the OpenAI SDK uses `status`, the
        // SBG gateway errors use `statusCode`. Accept either.
        const status = numericStatus(outer.status) ?? numericStatus(outer.statusCode);
        const code = stringField(outer.code) ?? stringField(nested?.code);
        const name = stringField(outer.name);
      
        if (
          status === 429 ||
          code === "rate_limit_exceeded" ||
          code === "too_many_requests" ||
          code === "RATE_LIMIT_ERROR" ||
          code === "QUOTA_EXCEEDED"
        ) {
          const retryAfterSeconds = parseRetryAfterSeconds(headerValue(outer.headers, "retry-after"));
          return new AppError(
            429,
            LLM_RATE_LIMITED,
            "The AI provider is temporarily rate-limited. Please try again shortly.",
            retryAfterSeconds === undefined ? null : { retryAfterSeconds },
          );
        }
      
        if (
          status === 408 ||
          code === "ETIMEDOUT" ||
          code === "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT" ||
          code === "TIMEOUT_ERROR" ||
          name === "AbortError" ||
          name === "APIConnectionTimeoutError"
        ) {
          return new AppError(503, LLM_TIMEOUT, "The AI provider timed out. Please try again.");
        }
      
        // Client-side request errors (4xx, excluding the timeout 408 and the
        // rate-limit 429 handled above) mean the request itself was rejected â€” bad
        // request, invalid/missing credentials, unsupported route. That is NOT a
        // provider outage: preserve the real status so failover layers do not burn
        // the fallback provider on a rejected request, and so callers see the real
        // status instead of a misleading 503.
        if (status !== null && status >= 400 && status < 500) {
          return new AppError(
            status,
            LLM_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE,
            "The AI provider rejected the request. Please check the request and try again.",
          );
        }
      
        return new AppError(
          503,
          LLM_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE,
          "The AI provider is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.",
        );
      }

        // Run Vitest-only tests separately because vi.mock() is incompatible with node --test.
        if (exitCode === 0 && (requestedTests.length === 0 || requestedVitestTests.length > 0)) {
          console.log("\nâ”€â”€ Running vitest tests (billing, checkout, ...) â”€â”€\n");
          exitCode = await new Promise((resolveRun) => {
            const vitestArgs = requestedVitestTests.length > 0
              ? ["run", "-c", "vitest.config.ts", ...requestedVitestTests]
              : ["run", "-c", "vitest.config.ts"];
            const child = spawn("vitest", vitestArgs, {
              cwd: apiRoot,
              stdio: "inherit",
              env: { ...process.env, ...testEnvironment, MONGODB_URI: getDatabaseUriForFile(), PATH: path },
              shell: true,
            });
            child.once("error", (error) => {
              console.error(`Unable to run vitest: ${error.message}`);
              resolveRun(1);
            });
            child.once("exit", (code) => resolveRun(code ?? 1));
          });
        }
      } finally {
        if (mongo) {
          await mongo.stop();
        }
      }
      process.exitCode = exitCode;

    import { MongoClient, ObjectId } from "mongodb";
    import { NvidiaNimChatAdapter } from "./src/providers/llm/nvidiaNimChat.adapter.ts";
    import { buildRagMessages } from "./src/modules/agents/answerWriter.service.ts";
    
    const question = process.env.PROBE_QUESTION;
    const task = process.env.PROBE_TASK;
    const limit = Number(process.env.PROBE_LIMIT || "10");
    if (!question || !task) throw new Error("PROBE_QUESTION and PROBE_TASK are required");
    
    const client = new MongoClient(process.env.MONGODB_URI);
    await client.connect();
    try {
      const db = client.db();
      const run = await db.collection("agentruns").findOne(
        { workflowName: "chat-rag-v1", "input.question": question },
        { sort: { createdAt: -1 } },
      );
      const step = await db.collection("agentsteps").findOne({
        runId: run?._id,
        agentName: "answer-writer-agent",
        action: "execute",
      });
      const ids = Array.isArray(step?.input?.approvedEvidenceIds)
        ? step.input.approvedEvidenceIds.slice(0, limit)
        : [];
      const chunks = await db.collection("documentchunks")
        .find({ _id: { $in: ids.map((id) => new ObjectId(id)) } })
        .toArray();
      const byId = new Map(chunks.map((chunk) => [String(chunk._id), chunk]));
      const sources = ids.flatMap((id) => {
        const chunk = byId.get(String(id));
        return chunk ? [{
          chunkId: String(chunk._id),
          documentId: String(chunk.documentId),
          text: chunk.text,
          pageNumber: chunk.pageNumber,
          sectionTitle: chunk.sectionTitle,
          documentTitle: "sql",
        }] : [];
      });
      const adapter = new NvidiaNimChatAdapter({
        apiKey: process.env.NVIDIA_API_KEY,
        baseUrl: process.env.NVIDIA_BASE_URL,
        model: process.env.NVIDIA_CHAT_MODEL,
        timeoutMs: Number(process.env.NVIDIA_TIMEOUT_MS || "20000"),
      });
      const startedAt = Date.now();
      const response = await adapter.complete({
        messages: buildRagMessages({
          citationsEnabled: true,
          sources,
          userMessage: question,
          task,
          language: "en",
        }),
        temperature: 0.3,
        maxTokens: task === "document_summary" ? 6144 : 3072,
        structuredOutput: { type: "json_object" },
      });
      console.log(JSON.stringify({
        question,
        task,
        sourceCount: sources.length,
        elapsedMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
        provider: response.provider,
        model: response.model,
        usage: response.usage,
        finishReason: response.choices[0]?.finishReason,
        content: response.choices[0]?.message?.content,
      }));
    } finally {
      await client.close();
    }

          inputKeys: step?.input && typeof step.input === "object" ? Object.keys(step.input) : null,
          outputKeys: step?.output && typeof step.output === "object" ? Object.keys(step.output) : null,
          inputSummary: step?.input && typeof step.input === "object"
            ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(step.input).map(([key, value]) => [
                key,
                Array.isArray(value) ? { type: "array", length: value.length, firstKeys: value[0] && typeof value[0] === "object" ? Object.keys(value[0]) : null } : typeof value,
              ]))
            : null,
          evidenceCount: Array.isArray(evidence) ? evidence.length : null,
          approvedChunkCount: chunks.length,
          approvedChunks: chunks.map((chunk) => ({
            id: String(chunk._id),
            pageNumber: chunk.pageNumber,
            text: typeof chunk.text === "string" ? chunk.text.slice(0, 360) : "",
          })),
          evidence: Array.isArray(evidence) ? evidence.map((item, index) => ({
            index: index + 1,
            chunkId: item.chunkId,
            pageNumber: item.pageNumber,
            title: item.documentTitle,
            text: typeof item.text === "string" ? item.text.slice(0, 280) : undefined,
          })) : evidence,
        }, null, 2));
      }
      await client.close();
      
      import mongoose from "mongoose";
      
      import AgentRunModel from "./src/db/models/agentRun.model.js";
      import AgentStepModel from "./src/db/models/agentStep.model.js";
      
      const uri = process.env.MONGODB_URI;
      if (!uri) throw new Error("MONGODB_URI is required");
      
      await mongoose.connect(uri);
      
      const run = await AgentRunModel.findOne({
        workflowName: "chat-rag-v1",
        status: "failed",
        "input.question": /summarize.*mysql/i,
      })
        .sort({ createdAt: -1 })
        .select("createdAt input status error latencyMs")
        .lean()
        .exec();
      
      if (!run) throw new Error("No matching failed RAG run found");
      
      const step = await AgentStepModel.findOne({
        runId: run._id,
        agentName: "citation-verification-agent",
        action: "execute",
      })
        .select("createdAt status error latencyMs input output")
        .lean()
        .exec();
      
      console.log(JSON.stringify({ run, step }, null, 2));
      await mongoose.disconnect();

            "pageNumber": 25,
            "text": "Installing & Logging\n• To Log into MySQL\n$ mysql -h hostname -u username –p\n• you should get a response something like this:\nEnter password:\nOSD 33"
          },
          {
            "rank": 2,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf8510c",
            "pageNumber": 24,
            "text": "How MySQL stores data?\n– A MySQL server can store several databases\n– Databases are stored as directories\n• Default is at /usr/local/mysql/var/\n• Or /var/lib/mysql (Ubuntu /Debian)\n– Tables are stored as files inside each database (directory)\nOSD 31"
          },
          {
            "rank": 3,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850f9",
            "pageNumber": 5,
            "text": "History of MySQL\n• Sun Microsystems acquired MySQL AB on 26 February 2008 for approximately $1\nbillion.\n• Oracle Corporation then acquired Sun in 2010 for $5.6 billion.\n• The day Oracle announced the purchase of Sun, Michael \"Monty\" Widenius forked\nMySQL, launching MariaDB, and took a swath of MySQL developers with him\n• MariaDB is a community-developed fork"
          },
          {
            "rank": 4,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850fa",
            "pageNumber": 6,
            "text": "History of MySQL\n• MySQL Enterprise Server\nAvailable only with the MySQL Enterprise subscription.\nAnnual Subscription USD 5,000-10,000\n• MySQL Community Server\nThe MySQL database server for open source developers and technology\nenthusiasts who want to get started with MySQL. Supported by the large MySQL\nopen source community. that is free of charge.\nOSD 8"
          },
          {
            "rank": 5,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf8510b",
            "pageNumber": 23,
            "text": "MySQL Terminology\n• Mysql is an interactive client that lets you issue queries and see the results.\n• Two administrative clients are:\n– mysqldump, a backup program that dumps table contents into a file.\n– mysqladmin, which enables you to check on the status of the server and performs other\nadministrative tasks such as telling the server to shut down.\nOSD 30"
          },
          {
            "rank": 6,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850f5",
            "pageNumber": 1,
            "text": "hd\n1 MySQL |\nopen somes ~The\nOPENSOURCE"
          },
          {
            "rank": 7,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850f8",
            "pageNumber": 4,
            "text": "History of MySQL\n• Original development of MySQL by Michael Widenius and David Axmark beginning\nin 1994 and First internal release on 23 May 1995.\n• He has a daughter My (after whom MySQL was named)\n• Michael Widenius founding the MySQL AB (company in Swedish)\nOSD 6\nhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Widenius\nhttps://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/histor"
          },
          {
            "rank": 8,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850f6",
            "pageNumber": 2,
            "text": "Day 1 Contents\n• Why MySQL?\n• History of MySQL.\n• RDBMS concepts and terminology\n• Installing & Logging.\n• Creating Users and maintaining their privileges.\n• DDL (CREATE DB/TABLE, ALTER, DROP,….)\n• Columns Data Types\n• Indexing\nOSD 3"
          },
          {
            "rank": 9,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf85109",
            "pageNumber": 21,
            "text": "Installing\n● For Ubuntu/Debian :\n$ sudo apt-get install mariadb-server\n● For CentOS/Red Hat Distros:\n$ sudo yum install mariadb-server\n$ sudo systemctl enable mariadb\n$ sudo systemctl start mariadb\nOSD 27"
          },
          {
            "rank": 10,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf8510a",
            "pageNumber": 22,
            "text": "MySQL Terminology - CLIENT/SERVER ARCTICTURE\n● MySQL operates using a client/server architecture.\n● The server (mysqld) runs on the machine where your databases are stored. It\nlistens for client requests on port 3306.\nOSD 28"
          },
          {
            "rank": 11,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850f7",
            "pageNumber": 3,
            "text": "Why MySQL?\n• Designed for high volume environments.\n• Cross platform\n• Low / No Cost.\n• Stability\n• Open Source\nOSD 4\nhttps://www.mysql.com/why-mysql/case-studies/\nhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_relational_database_management_systems"
          },
          {
            "rank": 12,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf850fb",
            "pageNumber": 7,
            "text": "Why MySQL?\n• Performance\n– http://www.mysql.com/why-mysql/benchmarks/\nOSD 10"
          },
          {
            "rank": 13,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf85106",
            "pageNumber": 18,
            "text": "ERD Symbols and Notations\nOSD 23\n• Derived Attribute\nAn attribute based on another attribute. This is found rarely in ER diagrams. Such as calculations\nSUCH AS call duration, age.\n• Relationship\nA relationship describes how entities interact.\nExample: Student, address, track, staff, courses, desk"
          },
          {
            "rank": 14,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf8512b",
            "pageNumber": 55,
            "text": "Creating Indexes\n• If you find that you are running many queries on a column that is not a key, you\nmay want to add an index on that column to improve performance.\nCREATE INDEX index_name\nON table_name (index_column_name , ...])\nOSD 68"
          },
          {
            "rank": 15,
            "id": "6a892a29f7bf4eb62bf85170",
            "pageNumber": 1,
            "text": "Abdallah Adel Abdelgwad Abdelhakem\nTel: 01553979226 | Minya, Egypt | Abdallah.adel.abdelgwad@gmail.com\nGitHub: Abdallahadel2004 | LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/abdallah-adel-92901722a/ | Military Status : Currently serving\nSUMMARY\nFull-Stack Software Engineer and current trainee at the Information Technology Institute (ITI) Professional Training Prog"
          },
          {

            "pageNumber": 38,
            "text": "Creating Databases\n• At the MySQL command prompt, type\nCREATE DATABASE db_name;\n• You should see a response like this :\nQuery OK, 1 row affected (0.0 sec).\n• Statement must end with (‘;’). The semicolon tells mysql that the statement is\ncomplete. Another way to terminate a statement is to use \\g (“go”) rather than a\nsemicolon.\nOSD 48"
          },
          {
            "rank": 17,
            "id": "6a88fd81f7bf4eb62bf8510e",
            "pageNumber": 26,
            "text": "INVOKING CLIENT PROGRAMS\n● You can exit mysql client using\nmysql> exit\nmysql>quit\nmysql>\\q\n• The default statement terminators are: \\g and ;\n● The \\G is also recognized s statement terminator, It displays the result in a vertical\nstyle:\nmysql> SELECT VERSION(), DATABASE()\\G\nOSD 34"

    $ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe" -Command "Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath 'api/Dockerfile'; Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath 'docker-compose.yml' | Select-String -Pattern 'command|entrypoint' -Context 2,2"
    status: Completed · exit 0
      FROM node:22-bookworm-slim
      
      WORKDIR /repo
      
      COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
      COPY api/package.json api/package.json
      COPY app/package.json app/package.json
      COPY workers/package.json workers/package.json
      
      RUN apt-get update \
          && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates \
          && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
      
      ENV MONGOMS_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL=1
      RUN npm ci --workspace api --workspace workers --include-workspace-root --ignore-scripts \
          && npm rebuild argon2 \
          && npm install @esbuild/linux-x64 --no-save
      
      COPY tsconfig.base.json eslint.config.mjs ./
      COPY workers/ workers/
      RUN npm run build --workspace workers
      
      COPY api/ api/
      
      WORKDIR /repo/api
      
      EXPOSE 5000
      
      CMD ["npm", "run", "dev"]
      
      
      > services:
        api:

      function extractConfirmationValue(text: string): string | null {
        const normalized = normalizeNumericText(text).toLowerCase();
        const isDeicticConfirmation =
          /^\s*(?:so|then|and|ok|okay|meaning|so\s+it\s+is)\b/u.test(normalized) &&
          /\b(?:hours?|hrs?|h|days?|minutes?|min|seconds?|sec|percent|%)\b/u.test(normalized) &&

        if (!isDeicticConfirmation) return null;
        const match =

      function preserveDirectTierContrast(

      /**
